text:
Anya: quick heads-up — seeing a ~12% p95 regression on small-chat after the AWQ packer change (PR #4752). baseline vs post-deploy: p50 42ms -> 44ms, p95 128ms -> 143ms, throughput steady. :frowning:
Marc: can you drop the perf run or flamegraph? which kernel ended up being used for the hot layers?
Anya: pasted snippets from the runtime logs and a short diff below. kernel chooser shows several layers falling back from `awq-int8-fast` -> `awq-int8-serial`. kv cache hit rate in traces also dipped 0.98 -> 0.91 for these requests.
Anya: ```
kernel_choice: layer16 -> awq-int8-serial (expected awq-int8-fast)
kvcache.hit_rate: 0.98 -> 0.91
pack.alignment: 16 -> 8
group_size: 32 -> 16 (auto)
```
Sree: why did pack alignment/group size change? PR 4752 wasn't supposed to touch pack alignment afaik. :thinking:
Diego: PR touched the packer heuristics to reduce working set by ~6% — it added a dynamic group rebalance that can reduce group_size from 32 -> 16 for weight-only when sparsity/zero-fill crosses a threshold. the intent was memory, not perf regression.
Lauren: can someone repro locally? quick command I use: `./perf/run_client --model owl-awq-int8 --group-size 32 --pack-mode legacy --concurrency 4`
Marc: ran a local microbench (same model/inputs):
- group 32: p95 140ms, pack CPU 4.0ms
- group 16: p95 152ms, pack CPU 4.7ms
So packing overhead + memcpy/align takes ~0.7ms more and p95 moved accordingly. kernel dispatch also incurred +9% overhead in the 16 case.
Anya: traced hotpath with `trace:kv:hotpath` — packer added an extra memcpy path for non-16 alignment which pushes some requests off the fast KV-aligned path. that explains the lower kv-hit-like behaviour (more micro-moves, less cache affinity).
perf-bot: flamegraph uploaded: https://perf.internal/runs/3112345678/flame (uploaded) :eyes:
Sree: two options: (1) revert the rebalance change and find a different memory optimization, or (2) make the packer preserve 16-byte alignment for weight-only int8 kernels and only apply rebalance when `pack.force_mem_savings=true`.
Diego: plan: add a conservative alignment override if `kernel.hint=awq-int8-fast` so we don't change the alignment that the kernel expects. i can put up a canary patch.
Lauren: also double-check if batching heuristics amplify this — more small requests (batch size 1/2) will pay the extra pack penalty frequently. check `batching.avg_size` and `kv.prefetch` stats while running the canary.
Marc: i'll run a small matrix overnight: group_size in [32,24,16], pack_align in [16,8], kernel_hint in [fast,serial], batch_size in [1,4,8]. will post results tomorrow AM.
Anya: thanks. if canary looks good i prefer to revert the rebalance and reintroduce memory savings as an opt-in flag. we should also add a unit test that asserts pack alignment for weight-only kernels doesn’t change unexpectedly. :+1:
Diego: noted — i'll add the override + test and open a PR against canary.
Sree: one more ask — capture a KV cache trace before/after with `kv.trace=1` and include `pack.stats=true` in the trace blob. it'll make root-cause obvious.
Anya: added to checklist. will attach traces to the PR. thanks all.
Marc: cool — will post the overnight matrix results here. :thumbsup:
